label: r4c1
name: best net, 64 minibatches
hypothesis: Same as r3c2, but with 64 minibatches of 64 samples instead of 32 of 128. That doubles the gradient steps per update again while the sample count stays near 225k. Going from 16 to 32 minibatches raised dev success from 0.63 to 0.89, and training success was still rising, so gradient steps still seem to be the limit. Refuted if the 2-seed dev mean falls below about 0.85.
last_analysis: Every observed target is shifted by X/2 columns. Rolling the input to undo that shift is what took dev success from 0 to about 0.6 (r1c1, r1c2). After that, the recipe mattered more than the architecture. Doubling the minibatches from 16 to 32 raised the score from 0.63 to 0.89 (r3c2, both seeds above 0.85), which is well beyond the seed spread. Raising entropy from 0.02 to 0.04 at 16 minibatches gave 0.74, a likely gain of about 0.1. Changes that made the network wider or the head more complex scored worse (r1c3, r2c1, r3c1). Using 1 PPO epoch or a longer horizon hurt badly (r2c2, r2c3). So the limit is gradient steps per sample plus early exploration, not network capacity. The remaining failures are wrong upper-layer bricks on tall stacks and early DONE, and training success was still rising at the end. This last round keeps the r3c2 network and tests: 64 minibatches alone, entropy 0.04 at 32 minibatches, and both together.
